title: Off the Grid
desc: Micronations, shifting borders & geographical freaks of nature

questions.q: Sealand is a self-proclaimed micronation built on what, off the coast of England?
questions.a: An abandoned WWII sea fort (HM Fort Roughs) in the North Sea

questions.q: What is the least visited country in the world by tourists?
Lake Baikal in Russia holds what percentage of the world's surface fresh water?
questions.a: About 20% — it's the deepest and oldest lake on Earth

questions.q: Which capital city was purpose-built in the 1960s to move the government away from the coast?
questions.a: Brasília, Brazil — inaugurated in 1960, designed by Oscar Niemeyer and Lúcio Costa

questions.q: The border between Belgium and the Netherlands passes through houses, cafes, and even a front door. What's the town?
questions.a: Baarle — specifically Baarle-Hertog (Belgian) and Baarle-Nassau (Dutch), an insane patchwork of enclaves

questions.q: What natural phenomenon causes the Sahara Desert to fertilise the Amazon Rainforest?
questions.a: Dust storms — phosphorus-rich dust from the Bodélé Depression in Chad is carried across the Atlantic by wind

questions.q: Which landlocked country has the world's largest navy by number of personnel?
questions.a: None sensibly do — but Bolivia, Laos, and several others maintain small naval forces on rivers and lakes. The question is a trap

questions.q: What is the Ring of Fire?
questions.a: A horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific Ocean where about 75% of the world's volcanic eruptions and 90% of earthquakes occur

questions.q: Greenland is the world's largest island. But most of its land mass is covered by what?
questions.a: An ice sheet up to 3km thick — if it all melted, global sea levels would rise about 7 metres

questions.q: What is special about the town of Coober Pedy in Australia?
questions.a: Most residents live underground — in converted opal mines — to escape temperatures that regularly exceed 40°C
